'''Siobhán Vernon''' (née O'Shea) was the first Irish-born woman to obtain a PhD in pure mathematics in Ireland, in 1964.<ref>{{cite web|title=Siobhán Vernon|url=http://cardcolm.org/Atlas.html#VernonSiobhan|website=Atlas of Irish Mathematics & Mathematicians|access-date=12 March 2017}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Siobhán O'Shea was born in [[Macroom]], County Cork in 1932 and was the daughter of Joseph J. O'Shea and his wife M. O'Shea.<ref name=mactutor>{{MacTutor Biography|id=Vernon}}</ref>

Her post-primary education was at the Convent of Mercy in Macroom, but she also attended the De La Salle, a secondary school for boys, for the higher level mathematics classes required for the Irish [[Leaving Certificate (Ireland)|Leaving Certificate]] examination. She entered [[University College Cork|University College, Cork]] in 1949 and was awarded a college scholarship in 1950, based on the results of her first year examinations.  She graduated in 1952 with a first class honours B.Sc. in Mathematics and Mathematical Physics. She went on to complete her M.Sc. in Mathematics and Mathematics Statistics, awarded in 1954.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.irishtimes.com/opinion/letters/appreciation-dr-siobhan-vernon-1.1110760|title=Appreciation Dr Siobhan Vernon|date=31 December 2002|work=The Irish Times|access-date=12 March 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Siobhán Vernon worked as a demonstrator in the Department of Mathematics at University College, Cork while she completed her M.Sc. and was then appointed Senior Demonstrator.<ref name=mactutor/> Encouraged by Dr Patrick Brendan Kennedy, Siobhán began to publish research in 1956 and was appointed to the full-time post of Assistant in 1957. Continuing her research career, she spent a year as a visiting lecturer in [[Royal Holloway, University of London|Royal Holloway College]], University of London, in 1962-63.<ref name=":1" />

Returning to University College, Cork, she submitted her published papers for the award of PhD, which was awarded in 1964 by the [[National University of Ireland]]. She was appointed lecturer in 1965.<ref name=":1" />

Following her marriage to geologist Peter Vernon, Siobhán reduced her teaching to half-time, as they raised their four children. She later returned to full time teaching, retiring in 1988.<ref name=mactutor/>

== Awards ==
In 1995 she was honoured with a Catherine McAuley award as a distinguished past pupil by the Convent of Mercy in Macroom.<ref name=":1" />

== Later life and death ==
Her final publication came after her retirement, when she contributed a chapter on Paddy Kennedy in Creators of Mathematics: The Irish Connection.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Long|first=Maebh|year=2007|title=Irish Mathematicians|url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/resources/kaleidoscope/issue1volume1/Kaleidoscope_Long_1.1_Irishmaths.pdf|journal=Kaleidoscope|volume=1.1|pages=3}}</ref> She died on 18 September 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ucc.ie/archive/courier/courierWin2002.pdf|title=Dr Siobhán Vernon Obituary|last=Barry|first=Patrick D.|date=Winter 2002|website=The College Courier}}</ref>
